text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mubarak to discuss with Kohl tomorrow economic cooperation and Europe's role in reviving Middle East peace process. President to arrive in Germany today.
- Clinton's national security adviser says Clinton will not intervene to give peace process a push. Israel warns it will cancel residency of 50,000 Palestinians from Jerusalem who live abroad.
- Mubarak and Arafat to meet in Cairo this week to discuss Middle East peace process.
- Cabinet to discuss on Wednesday economic results of Egyptian-Moroccan summit.
- Local Administration minister says investors across the country applied to carry out 319 projects during April worth about $4 billion.
- Private companies will for the first time calculate tariffs.
- Foreign Ministry source says Egypt hopes Zaire will now be stable.
- Egyptian-Syrian joint committee to meet next Monday.
- Djibouti president arrives in Egypt for two-day visit.
- Egyptian-Kuwaiti company share offer three times oversubscribed.
- Foreign Minister Moussa says Israel threatens Arab security. He says attacks on southern Lebanon affirm Israel's wrong interpretation of peace.
- Contacts underway to secure release of seven Egyptian fishermen being detained in Israel.
